assets.narration_text: I built a 10-slide deck in 60 seconds with Tome AI—no design skills, no templates. But before you ditch PowerPoint forever… watch this. 1️⃣ **Zero Design Skills Needed**: Type a prompt, get polished slides with AI-generated visuals. 2️⃣ **Free Tier Actually Works**: Unlike most ‘free’ tools, Tome’s basic plan lets you export without watermarks. 3️⃣ **The Catch**: Offline mode? Forget it. No internet = no slides. And customization? Limited compared to PowerPoint’s 30 years of features. Try Tome AI free (link below) and tell me—does this replace PowerPoint for you? Also, check out our video on AI tools that *actually* save time for more like this!

assets.narration_text: Last week I ran the same research task through Perplexity Pro, ChatGPT-4o, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Perplexity didn’t just finish 3x faster—it surfaced three academic papers the others missed, all published in the last 48 hours. That’s not a fluency edge; that’s a real-time data moat. And here’s the kicker: the feature that made the difference isn’t even the one they advertise. Perplexity was built by a team of ex-Google, Meta, and Quora engineers who were frustrated by the same problem: search engines give you links, not answers. They launched in 2022 with a simple premise—what if an AI could synthesize information from the web in real time, with citations, and do it faster than you can open a new tab? The company is now valued at over $1 billion, backed by Jeff Bezos and Nvidia, and they’re not just competing with Google—they’re gunning for the entire $300 billion search market. Perplexity is a conversational search engine. You ask a question, and it returns a concise answer with footnotes to sources. But here’s the breakdown of what’s under the hood: 1) Real-time web indexing—it crawls the live web, not just pre-2023 data like most LLMs. 2) Focus mode—you can toggle between academic papers, Reddit threads, or YouTube transcripts. 3) Threads—like a chat history, but with every response linked to its sources. 4) Pro version ($20/month) unlocks GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, and their own experimental model, which they claim outperforms both on niche queries. It’s available as a web app, iOS app, and Chrome extension. I tested Perplexity across four specific use-cases: 1) **Academic research**: For my recent video on AI ethics, Perplexity Pro found 7 peer-reviewed papers from 2024 that Google Scholar didn’t surface. The catch? It sometimes misinterprets methodology—you still need to read the papers. 2) **Product research**: When I was comparing noise-canceling headphones, Perplexity pulled real-time pricing from 12 retailers and summarized Reddit threads on durability. But it missed some niche forums, like Head-Fi. 3) **Coding help**: It’s great for explaining error messages with up-to-date Stack Overflow threads. But for complex debugging, GitHub Copilot still wins—Perplexity’s code snippets are hit or miss. 4) **Travel planning**: It generated a 3-day itinerary for Kyoto with restaurant reservations and train times. The surprise? It included a warning about a local festival that would’ve made hotels 3x more expensive—something Google Travel missed. The biggest letdown? **Creative writing**. Perplexity’s answers are too sterile for storytelling. It’s a researcher, not a muse. 1) **Paywall blindness**: Perplexity can’t access paywalled content, so if the answer is behind a Nature or IEEE subscription, it’ll either miss it or hallucinate. 2) **Citation overload**: For broad questions like ‘What is quantum computing?’, it’ll dump 20 sources on you—overwhelming, not helpful. 3) **No image generation**: Unlike ChatGPT, you can’t ask it to create a diagram or edit a photo. 4) **Privacy trade-offs**: Your queries are logged for 30 days, even on Pro. If you’re researching sensitive topics, this is a dealbreaker. 5) **Mobile app quirks**: The iOS app crashes if you paste a long query, and the voice search is glitchy—it cut me off mid-sentence twice. Perplexity isn’t replacing Google or ChatGPT—it’s carving out a new category. If you’re a student, journalist, or professional who needs to synthesize information fast, the Pro version is worth the $20/month. For everyone else, the free tier is still a powerful tool, but with limitations. The real magic isn’t the answers; it’s the **real-time sourcing**. That’s the feature ChatGPT can’t match, and it’s why Perplexity is the only AI tool I’ve paid for this year. If you’re curious about how it stacks up against other AI tools, I did a deep dive on [cross_promotion]—check it out for the full comparison.
